messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC priors for betabinomial and gev likelihoods
parts:
Neither a sharp prior nor a fixed value helps. What works is a spatio-temporal (ar1) random effect, and/or a random group effect with fixed precision. The ar1 parameter comes out as .998. I modify to rw1, but then the gsl-trouble returns. Likewise when the precision of the random group effect is made variable. 

What is going on here? To me it seems that some missing constraint allow the routine to enter a "black hole" from which nothing sensible comes out. With a clear idea of the problem it might be easier to find a workaround.

In addition I wonder, do I specify the sharp prior correctly?

control.family = list(hyper = list(rho = list(prior = "normal", param = c(0.3,10), initial = 0.3)))

best
Øyvind

Thanks, Håvard

I managed to proceed by leaving out all sophisticated issues of the previous betabinomial model. But when combined with a gaussian model. The problem is back again. The betabinoimial data has now values in [0,1] with a mix of 0-s, 1-s and in-betweens (Ntrials = 1). An atemporal spde-field and some fixed effects (including a time trend) predicts the binomial data. In addition there is gaussian data which is predicted with a scaled copy of the spde-field and fixed effects.

I have experimented with sharp priors and fixed values on some of the five hyperparameters, but with no success. Gsl-errors arise when optimum approaches. One trial led as far as the Hessian (see below), which is horrible.
How can this be avoided? There are no more simplifications to make.

best
Øyvind

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC priors for betabinomial and gev likelihoods
parts:
I have tried beta, but INLA does not accept 0-s and 1-s as beta-distributed data, which actually seems sensible to me. The beta-density is either 0 or INF at an end point. In my case the density is necessarily INF because of overdispersion.

The binomial nature of the beta-binomial is precisely why it works for both 0-s and 1-s. I have been wrong in accepting in-between values in this case, though. The betabinomial seems well defined as a continuous density for continuous N > 1. See: http://ac.inf.elte.hu/Vol_039_2013/137_39.pdf. Hence, Ntrials need to be larger than 1. But what does actually INLA do with non-integer values of Ntrials and x? Follow the paper largely, or something else?

best
Øyvind
